definition_zh: 弄错的；判断错的；错误的；被误认的
definition_en: wrong in one's own judgement or belief, or wrongly identified by other people
core_image: 两个人背对背站着，胸前的名牌却被贴到了对方身上
scene: 站台上人流涌动，接站的人手里只有一张模糊的旧照片。 At the busy exit, the driver waved at the wrong passenger because he was mistaken about the old photograph.
sceneCN: 这里是「弄错的」（第 1 个义项：自己判断有误，常用 be mistaken 表示弄错）；句意为出口人太多，司机凭那张旧照片认错了人，向陌生乘客招手。图中可辨识物件：接站纸牌、旧照片、行李箱。

pos.zh: 弄错的；错误的；被误认的

derivatives.zh: 由 mistaken 加 -ly 构成，义为「错误地；误以为」
由 un- 加 mistake 加 -able 构成，指清楚得不会被认错

senses.title: Holding a wrong opinion about something
senses.definition: having formed a belief or opinion that does not match the facts, used especially after the verb be
senses.definitionCN: 形成了与事实不符的看法或判断，尤用于动词 be 之后
senses.example: You are mistaken if you believe the library closes at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你以为图书馆中午关门，那你就弄错了。
senses.why: Mistaken is the past participle of mistake, so it describes someone who has already made the wrong taking and still carries its result; the pattern with be keeps the person, not the fact, at the centre.
senses.whyCN: mistaken 是 mistake 的过去分词，说的是一个人已经做完了那次「拿错」，并且还带着结果；be 加 mistaken 的句式把「人」而不是「事」放在句子中心，所以它表示的是人弄错了。

senses.title: Based on a wrong belief
senses.definition: describing a belief, plan or method that rests on an error and is therefore likely to fail
senses.definitionCN: 形容建立在错误之上的看法、计划或做法，因而多半会失败
senses.example: The rescue team searched the wrong valley on a mistaken assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队基于一个错误的假设，搜错了山谷。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the participle stops describing the person and starts describing what the person trusts, so the error moves from a mind into a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词放在名词前面时，不再描述人，而描述人所信赖的东西；错误于是从一个人的脑子里搬进了一份计划里。

senses.title: Identified wrongly by other people
senses.definition: describing a person or thing that others have taken for someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 形容被别人认成了另一个人或另一件东西
senses.example: The apology came after a case of mistaken identity at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 机场发生身份误认之后，才有了那声道歉。
senses.why: Here the participle turns outward: the person did not err, others erred about him, and the fixed phrase mistaken identity names exactly that error made in the opposite direction.
senses.whyCN: 这里分词转向了外面：出错的不再是本人，而是别人把他认错了；mistaken identity 这个固定说法命名的正是这种反方向的错误。

intro.en: Mistaken is the past participle of mistake, a Norse verb of taking wrongly, and it became an adjective in its own right in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: mistaken 是 mistake 的过去分词，而 mistake 是古诺斯语中「拿错」的动词；十六世纪它自立为形容词。

items.en: The source verb mistaka combined mis-, wrongly, with taka, to take, and described a wrong grasp or a misjudged matter.
items.cn: 来源动词 mistaka 把 mis-（错）与 taka（拿）合在一起，描述抓错东西或判断错事情。

items.en: English took the verb as mistaken, whose past participle carried the meaning of having taken or understood wrongly.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词借来写作 mistaken，它的过去分词带有「已经拿错、已经理解错」的意思。

items.en: The participle began to stand alone after be, so that a person could be described as mistaken rather than as having mistaken something.
items.cn: 这个分词开始单独用在 be 之后，于是可以直接说一个人「弄错了」，而不必说他弄错了某件事。

items.en: Attributive uses such as a mistaken belief spread, and mistaken identity became a fixed phrase in law and in newspapers; this dating is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: a mistaken belief 这类定语用法流行开来，mistaken identity 也成为法律与新闻里的固定说法；这一时间点是一般认为，而非确证。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for wrong opinions, wrong plans and people wrongly named by others, while the participle use survives alongside.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指错误的看法、错误的计划，以及被别人叫错身份的人；分词用法则与它并存。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the verb it came from, one of its forms and the shared prefix; the near-meaning group holds adjectives of being wrong.
note.cn: 形近组收它所出的动词、该动词的一个形式以及共用的前缀；近义组收表示「不正确」的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb and noun from which the participle comes, meaning to take wrongly or the wrong act itself.
entries.definitionCN: mistaken 所出的动词与名词，指拿错或错误本身。

entries.definition: The past tense of mistake, the single act that leaves someone mistaken.
entries.definitionCN: mistake 的过去式，正是那一次造成「弄错」的动作。

entries.definition: The prefix for wrongly that sits inside both mistake and mistaken.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地」的前缀，同时嵌在 mistake 与 mistaken 里。

entries.definition: Not correct, used of answers, ideas and actions alike.
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的，可用于答案、想法与行为。

entries.definition: Not true or not according to a standard, a politer word than wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实或不合标准，比 wrong 更客气。

entries.definition: Based on a wrong judgement, often said of well-meaning people.
entries.definitionCN: 基于错误判断，常指出于好意的人。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is a participle that learned to stand alone, and it keeps pointing at a wrong taking somewhere behind the person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词是一个学会独立站立的过去分词，始终指向人背后那一次拿错。

normal.en: Mistaken is the participle of mistake, so the adjective always looks back at an act that has already happened.
normal.cn: mistaken 是 mistake 的分词，所以这个形容词总是回望一件已经发生过的动作。

normal.en: Be mistaken puts the person first: you are the one holding the wrong view.
normal.cn: be mistaken 把人放在前面：拿着错看法的是你本人。

normal.en: A mistaken belief moves the same error into the thing believed, which is why the adjective can sit before a noun.
normal.cn: a mistaken belief 把同样的错误挪进被相信的东西里，所以这个形容词可以放在名词前。

normal.en: Mistaken identity reverses the direction: the error is made by others about the person.
normal.cn: mistaken identity 把方向倒过来：错误是别人对这个人犯下的。

normal.en: Mistakenly adds -ly and describes how an action was done, not what someone is.
normal.cn: mistakenly 加 -ly，描述一个动作是怎么做的，而不是某人是什么状态。

abstract.en: To be mistaken is to be caught inside one's own certainty, which is why the word so often follows a direct address.
abstract.cn: be mistaken 意味着被困在自己的确信里，所以这个词常出现在直呼对方的句子里。

abstract.en: A mistaken belief is more dangerous than a simple error because it has a plan attached to it.
abstract.cn: 错误的看法比单纯的错误更危险，因为它后面挂着一份计划。

abstract.en: Mistaken identity shows that an error can belong to the watcher rather than to the person watched.
abstract.cn: mistaken identity 说明错误可以属于观看的人，而不属于被看的人。

examples.en: You are mistaken about the date of the meeting.
examples.cn: 你把会议日期弄错了。

examples.en: The plan failed because it rested on a mistaken belief.
examples.cn: 这个计划失败，是因为它建立在错误的看法上。

examples.en: The court case collapsed over mistaken identity.
examples.cn: 那桩案子因身份误认而不了了之。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷死忒肯」——迷糊到极点还死肯着自己的说法不改，就是弄错了。

root: mistaken 由 mistake 的过去分词转来：古诺斯语 mistaka（mis-「错」+ taka「拿」）；作形容词一般认为始于十六世纪，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: One participle covers a person who holds a wrong view, a belief built on that view, and a person whom others have named wrongly.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个分词覆盖三种情形：人自己抱着错看法，某种看法建立在错之上，以及一个人被别人叫错了身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man wearing someone else's name tag and acting on it with full confidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人挂着别人的名牌，还照着它自信地行事。

branches.en: a listener still holding the wrong date in mind
branches.cn: 听者心里还揣着错误的日期

branches.en: a plan drawn on a map of the wrong valley
branches.cn: 照着错山谷的地图画的计划

branches.en: a passenger waved at by the wrong driver
branches.cn: 被陌生司机招手的乘客

branches.en: a confident note written on a false premise
branches.cn: 在错误前提上写下的笃定批注

branches.en: two names exchanged on a luggage tag
branches.cn: 行李牌上被互换的两个名字

intro.en: The word is a Norse verb of wrong taking, its participle ending, and two English affixes that build the adverb and the negative adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「拿错」的古诺斯语动词、它的分词词尾，以及两个造出副词与否定的形容词的英语词缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mistaken; its stem is the Norse verb of taking, not a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: mistaken 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的词干是古诺斯语的「拿取」动词，而不是拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 驱散；使散开
definition_en: to throw things over an area or to make a group move apart
core_image: 一阵风把桌上的纸页吹得漫天飞舞，四处落下
scene: 风把桌上的纸张吹得四散。 The wind scattered the papers across the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 scatter 是「使散开」（第 2 个义项）；句意：风把纸张吹散在桌上。

derivatives.zh: 分散的；零星的
散射；分散
散射体；散布者
心不在焉的人

senses.title: Throw over an area
senses.definition: to throw small things over a surface or area
senses.definitionCN: 把小东西抛撒在一个表面或区域上
senses.example: She scattered seeds across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她把种子撒遍田地。
senses.why: The concrete sense is distributing small objects widely.
senses.whyCN: 具体义是把小物件广泛分布。

senses.title: Drive a group apart
senses.definition: to make a group of people or animals move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 使一群人或动物朝不同方向散开
senses.example: The police scattered the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 警察驱散了人群。
senses.why: Objects spreading apart become people driven apart.
senses.whyCN: 物件四散引申为人被驱散。

senses.title: Break up and spread
senses.definition: to separate and move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向移动
senses.example: The birds scattered when the cat appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 猫一出现，鸟群就散开了。
senses.why: The group itself can do the scattering.
senses.whyCN: 群体自身也可以执行散开的动作。

senses.title: Spread out data
senses.definition: to spread points or values over an area in statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在统计中把点或数值分散到某个区域
senses.example: The graph shows how the data scatter.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示了数据如何分散。
senses.why: The visual spread of points is called scatter.
senses.whyCN: 点的视觉分布被称为散点。

intro.en: Scatter is a Middle English word, perhaps related to shatter.
intro.cn: scatter 是中古英语词，可能与 shatter 有关。

items.en: A related form meant to disperse or sprinkle.
items.cn: 相关形式意为分散或撒播。

items.en: Scateren meant to throw about in all directions.
items.cn: scateren 意为向四面八方抛撒。

items.en: Scatter became common for crowds and seeds.
items.cn: scatter 广泛用于人群和种子。

items.en: Statistics adopted scatter for spread-out data.
items.cn: 统计学用 scatter 表示分散的数据。

items.en: Scatter covers physical, social, and statistical spread.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scatter 涵盖物理、社会与统计上的分散。

note.en: Scatter is compared with similar spellings and with words for spreading.
note.cn: 把 scatter 与形近词以及表示分散的词作比较。

entries.definition: to spread over a wide area
to scatter small drops or pieces

normalIntro.en: Scatter is the sound of small things flying apart.
normalIntro.cn: scatter 听起来就像小东西四散飞开。

normal.en: Scatter and shatter both suggest something breaking apart.
normal.cn: scatter 与 shatter 都暗示东西散裂。

normal.en: Sow seeds by scattering them over the soil.
normal.cn: 把种子撒在土壤上就是播种。

normal.en: The double t appears in scattered and scattering.
normal.cn: scattered 和 scattering 中有双写 t。

normal.en: Scatter the crowd means make it break up.
normal.cn: scatter the crowd 意为让人群散开。

normal.en: A scatter of houses means houses spread far apart.
normal.cn: a scatter of houses 意为房屋稀疏散布。

abstract.en: Scattering turns a single group into many directions.
abstract.cn: 分散把一个整体变成许多方向。

abstract.en: Ideas scatter more easily than seeds.
abstract.cn: 思想比种子更容易撒播。

abstract.en: What is scattered may never come back together.
abstract.cn: 散开的东西也许再也不会聚拢。

examples.en: He scattered the papers over the floor.
examples.cn: 他把纸张撒了一地。

examples.en: The wind scattered the leaves along the road.
examples.cn: 风把树叶吹散在路旁。

examples.en: The crowd scattered when the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨一开始，人群就散开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: scatter 与 shatter 形近，都含「散裂」之意；可记「一撒手，东西四散」。

root: 中古英语 scateren，可能与 shatter 同源，核心义「向四面八方抛撒、散开」。

sensesIntro.en: Scatter means to throw things widely, drive a group apart, spread out, or spread data.
sensesIntro.cn: scatter 意为广泛撒播、驱散群体、散开，或分散数据。

core.en: To send things apart in many directions.
core.cn: 把事物朝许多方向分开。

branches.en: The core act of throwing small things widely.
branches.cn: 广泛抛撒小物件的核心动作。

branches.en: A group is forced to break apart.
branches.cn: 群体被迫分散。

branches.en: A group separates by itself.
branches.cn: 群体自行分开。

branches.en: Data points spread across a graph.
branches.cn: 数据点在图上散布。

branches.en: Thrown objects and moving groups both spread.
branches.cn: 被抛之物与移动的群体都会散开。

intro.en: Scatter forms adjectives, nouns, and technical terms.
intro.cn: scatter 构成形容词、名词与技术术语。

latinIntro.en: Scatter is Germanic in origin, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: scatter 源自日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.example: A scattering of leaves covered the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上散落着零星的叶子。

items.example: My scatterbrain brother lost his keys.
items.exampleCN: 我心不在焉的弟弟丢了钥匙。

items.example: The scatter plot shows a trend.
items.exampleCN: 散点图显示出一种趋势。

definition_zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图
definition_en: the way in which parts of something are arranged; the arrangement of text and pictures on a page; a plan showing such an arrangement
core_image: 桌面上摊开的图纸，方块、线条和标注被摆成清楚的位置关系
scene: 设计师把桌上的草图推开一点，重新摆放照片和标题的位置。 The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
sceneCN: 这里是「版面布局」（第 1 个义项：各部分在页面上的安排）；句意是设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。图中可辨识物件：草图、照片、标题。

pos.zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图

derivatives.zh: 由 lay 与 out 组成的短语动词，义为「布置；摊开；排版」
由 re- 与 layout 复合而成，义为「重新布局」
由 lay out 的过去分词形式构成，义为「布置好的；摊开的」

senses.title: The arrangement of text and pictures on a page
senses.definition: the way text, pictures and empty space are arranged on a page or screen
senses.definitionCN: 文字、图片与空白在页面或屏幕上的安排方式
senses.example: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。
senses.why: Lay out first meant to spread things on a surface; printers then used it for placing type and images, and the noun kept that page sense.
senses.whyCN: lay out 最初指把东西摊在平面上；印刷者随后用它指摆放字与图，名词便保留了这层页面义。

senses.title: The way parts of a place are arranged
senses.definition: the arrangement of furniture, rooms or objects within a space
senses.definitionCN: 家具、房间或物件在某一空间内的安排
senses.example: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的新布局把水槽放到了窗下。
senses.why: A room is laid out much like a page: things are placed in relation to one another, and the same noun serves both.
senses.whyCN: 房间的布置很像页面的排版：物件按彼此关系摆放，同一个名词便兼指两者。

senses.title: A plan or diagram of an arrangement
senses.definition: a drawing or plan that shows how something is or will be arranged
senses.definitionCN: 表明某物现状或未来安排方式的图样或规划
senses.example: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师递给我们一张车间平面布置图。
senses.why: Once an arrangement is fixed, it can be drawn; the drawing takes the same name because it records the very placement the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 安排一旦确定就能画成图；图纸沿用同一个名字，因为它记录的正是这个词所描述的摆放方式。

intro.en: Layout is a nineteenth-century English compound: the verb lay out, meaning to spread or arrange, became a noun for the arrangement itself.
intro.cn: layout 是十九世纪的英语复合词：短语动词 lay out（摊开、布置）变成了指安排本身的名词。

items.en: Lay comes from the Old English verb lecgan, to put something down.
items.cn: lay 来自古英语动词 lecgan，意为把东西放下。

items.en: Middle English used lay out for spreading things on a surface.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lay out 表示把东西摊开在平面上。

items.en: The phrasal verb lay out came to mean arranging a room, a page or a plan.
items.cn: 短语动词 lay out 逐渐表示布置房间、排版或规划。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the two words were joined into the noun layout.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这两个词合并成名词 layout。

items.en: Modern English uses layout for pages, rooms, factories and computer screens.
items.cn: 现代英语用 layout 指页面、房间、工厂和电脑屏幕的布局。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of the phrasal verb and one compound with another meaning; the near-meaning group collects words for arrangement and design.
note.cn: 形近组收短语动词的各种形式和一个意义不同的复合词；近义组收表示安排与设计的词。

entries.definition: To spread something out or to arrange it according to a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西摊开，或按计划加以布置。

entries.definition: Arranged or spread out in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种方式布置好或摊开的。

entries.definition: An amount of money spent on something; the parts look alike but the meaning is different.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事花出的一笔钱；两个成分拼写相同，但词义不同。

entries.definition: A new or repeated arrangement of a page or space.
entries.definitionCN: 对页面或空间重新进行的布局。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order or in position.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被排成顺序或摆好位置的方式。

entries.definition: A plan or pattern made before something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 在建造之前拟定的计划或样式。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts to form a whole, especially in art.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分组成整体的安排，尤用于艺术。

entries.definition: The shape, size and general arrangement of a page or file.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的形状、尺寸与总体安排。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of a Germanic verb and a particle, and its senses all keep the idea of placing things into a plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个日耳曼语动词和一个副词小品词复合而成，各义项都保留「把东西放进计划」的想法。

normal.en: Lay out began as a verb meaning to spread things on a surface, and layout simply froze that action into a noun.
normal.cn: lay out 起初是动词，意为把东西摊在平面上，layout 则把这个动作凝固成名词。

normal.en: Page layout is the oldest noun sense: printers laid out type before they printed a sheet.
normal.cn: page layout 是最早的名词义：印刷者在印一张纸之前先摆放活字。

normal.en: Office layout and kitchen layout use the same idea on furniture and rooms instead of type and pictures.
normal.cn: office layout 和 kitchen layout 把同一想法用到家具和房间上，而不是字与图。

normal.en: A layout plan is the drawing of the arrangement, which is why the noun can also name a diagram.
normal.cn: layout plan 是布局的图纸，所以这个名词也能指一张图。

normal.en: Relayout adds re- to layout, so it means arranging the same space or page again.
normal.cn: relayout 在 layout 前加 re-，意为把同一空间或页面重新布置。

abstract.en: Layout is what turns a pile of things into a readable space, whether paper, room or factory.

abstract.en: A good layout is invisible: we notice it only when the parts refuse to fit.

examples.en: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.

examples.en: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.

examples.en: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.

definition_zh: 颌；下巴；（字面或比喻）下颚；（工具）钳口
definition_en: either of the two bones or parts that form the mouth and hold the teeth, or a gripping part of a tool
core_image: 一张脸的下半部，上下两排牙齿像两把钳子合上
scene: 老人慢慢嚼着面包，脸上的颌骨一起一落。 His jaw moved slowly as he chewed.
sceneCN: 这里 jaw 是「颌」（第 1 个义项：构成嘴部、承载牙齿的骨或部位），句意为他咀嚼时下颌慢慢动着。画面里的物件：面包、牙齿、老年斑的皮肤。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「上下颌」，也指机构的夹钳
由 jaw 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……颌的」，见于 long-jawed 等复合词
由 jaw 与 bone 复合，义为「颌骨」

senses.title: The bone that holds teeth
senses.definition: one of the two bony structures that form the frame of the mouth and hold the teeth
senses.definitionCN: 构成嘴部框架并承载牙齿的两块骨结构之一
senses.example: He broke his lower jaw in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛中摔断了下颌。
senses.why: The anatomical sense is the oldest and stays the basis for every later use.
senses.whyCN: 解剖义最古老，也是后来所有用法的基础。

senses.title: The lower part of the face
senses.definition: the lower part of the face, seen especially when it is large or firm
senses.definitionCN: 脸的下部，尤其指宽大或坚硬的形态
senses.example: A square jaw ran across the whole bottom of his face.
senses.exampleCN: 宽方的下巴横过他的脸底。
senses.why: The bone shapes the face, so people name the visible outline by the bone beneath.
senses.whyCN: 骨头撑出脸的形状，于是人们用底下的骨来称呼那道外轮廓。

senses.title: A gripping part of a tool
senses.definition: one of the two parts of a vice or wrench that close on an object
senses.definitionCN: 老虎钳或扳手上合拢夹物的两片之一
senses.example: Tighten the jaws of the vice around the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 把老虎钳的钳口夹紧管道。
senses.why: A tool grips with two facing surfaces exactly as a mouth bites with two jaws.
senses.whyCN: 工具用两片相对的面夹住东西，与嘴用上下颌咬住一模一样。

senses.title: Something that closes in
senses.definition: a dangerous opening or closing area, such as between waves or between rocks
senses.definitionCN: 危险的开合处，如巨浪之间或岩石之间
senses.example: The boat slipped into the jaws of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 小船滑进了风暴的夹口。
senses.why: The mouth image grows into any wide, closing gap that swallows what enters.
senses.whyCN: 嘴的意象扩大成任何张开又合拢、把东西吞进去的缺口。

senses.title: To talk on and on
senses.definition: used informally for talking at length, often about nothing important
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示长时间讲话，常指说些不重要的事
senses.example: They jawed about football all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整晚都在聊足球。
senses.why: The verb turns the jaw that does the working into the act of talking.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个干活的颌变成了说话这个动作。

intro.en: Jaw is an old French borrowing, from Old French joue, meaning cheek, reshaped in English toward the sound it names.
intro.cn: jaw 是从古法语借来的词，原形 joue 意为「面颊」，在英语里逐渐定型为现在的读音与拼写。

items.en: joue meant a cheek.
items.cn: joue 意为面颊。

items.en: English took the word as jawe or chaw, and it meant the part that holds teeth.
items.cn: 英语借入为 jawe 或 chaw，指承载牙齿的部位。

items.en: The spelling drifted toward jaw and the meaning settled on the bone.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐变成 jaw，词义固定在骨头上。

items.en: The tool sense appeared as machines with gripping parts spread.
items.cn: 随着带夹持部件的机器普及，工具义出现。

items.en: The informal verb to jaw, meaning to chatter, is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 口语动词 jaw「喋喋不休」在十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jaw- family; the near-meaning group holds words for mouth parts and gripping tools.
note.cn: 形近组是 jaw- 词族；近义组收嘴部器官与夹持工具相关词。

entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「令人瞠目结舌的」。

entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「下巴尖」，只指最外边的一点。

entries.definition: The side of the face below the eye.

entries.definition: A curved gripping part on an animal or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「爪」，指弯曲的夹持部位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Old French cheek into the bone, the vice, and the storm.

abstract.en: What opens wide will one day close.
abstract.cn: 张得很大的东西总有一天会合拢。

examples.en: He rubbed his jaw where the ball had hit him.
examples.cn: 他揉了揉被球打中的下巴。

examples.en: The crocodile opened its jaws and waited.
examples.cn: 鳄鱼张开嘴等着。

examples.cn: 他们在街角站着聊了一个小时。

definition_zh: 激怒；挑衅；引发；引起；煽动
definition_en: to stir someone into anger or action, or to cause a reaction or an event
core_image: 有人把一根长杆伸进静止的水面，圈圈波纹从杆尖向外荡开
scene: 这份提案把两边的旧账都翻了出来，会上争了两个小时。 The proposal provoked a long debate in the council.
sceneCN: 这里指引起一场争论（第 3 个义项：引发反应或讨论）；句意为这份提案在议会引发了长时间辩论。图中可辨识物件：伸进水面的长杆、向外荡开的波纹、静止的水；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅；激怒；诱因」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的；引人深思的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「挑衅地」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「气人的；惹人恼的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅者」（少用）

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to stir a person into anger, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 使某人动怒，常带故意成分
senses.example: His remarks provoked the crowd outside the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话激怒了厅外的人群。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to call forth, and anger is one of the things called out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「唤出」，而怒气正是从人身上被唤出来的东西之一。

senses.title: To challenge deliberately
senses.definition: to invite a fight or a strong reaction by confronting someone on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意顶撞某人，以招来争斗或强烈反应
senses.example: The guard was provoked into opening the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门卫被激得打开了大门。
senses.why: Provocation is a call the other person is expected to answer, which is why it feels like an invitation.
senses.whyCN: 挑衅是一声预期对方会回应的召唤，所以才像一份邀请。

senses.title: To give rise to a reaction
senses.definition: to cause a response, discussion or public reaction without any intent to anger
senses.definitionCN: 引起回应、讨论或公众反应，不含激怒意图
senses.example: The report provoked wide discussion in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在报界引发广泛讨论。
senses.why: The oldest neutral sense simply calls a response into being, with no emotional charge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的中性义只是把回应唤出来，不带情绪色彩。

senses.title: To arouse interest
senses.definition: to make curiosity or interest appear in someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生好奇或兴趣
senses.example: The strange photograph provoked her curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 那张奇怪的照片引起了她的好奇。
senses.why: Curiosity is another response that is called forth rather than pushed in.
senses.whyCN: 好奇也是被唤出的回应，而不是被塞进去的。

senses.title: To stir an emotion
senses.definition: to bring a strong feeling such as fear, pity or laughter to the surface
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧、怜悯或笑意等强烈情绪浮到表面
senses.example: The empty street provoked a sense of unease.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道激起一种不安。
senses.why: Emotions are treated as things that can be summoned, which is the core of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被当作可以召唤的东西，这正是拉丁动词的核心。

senses.title: To draw criticism
senses.definition: to cause disapproval, complaint or public objection
senses.definitionCN: 引起不满、投诉或公开反对
senses.example: The decision provoked protests from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定招致居民的抗议。
senses.why: Criticism is a response with a negative charge, but the mechanism is still calling forth.
senses.whyCN: 批评是一种带负电的回应，但机制仍是「唤出」。

senses.title: To trigger an attack or symptom
senses.definition: to set off a physical episode such as a cough, a fit or an allergic response
senses.definitionCN: 触发咳嗽、发作或过敏反应等身体事件
senses.example: Cold air provoked a coughing fit.
senses.exampleCN: 冷空气诱发了一阵咳嗽。
senses.why: Medicine uses the verb for anything that sets a latent condition going.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个动词指任何让潜伏状况启动的因素。

senses.title: To incite action
senses.definition: to urge a group towards collective action, often unrest
senses.definitionCN: 鼓动一群人采取集体行动，常指骚动
senses.example: leaflets provoked a march the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 传单煽动了第二天早上的游行。
senses.why: A crowd is called into motion, and the verb keeps the image of a call rather than a push.
senses.whyCN: 人群被唤起来行动，这个动词保留「召唤」而非「推动」的画面。

intro.en: Provoke comes from Latin provocare, to call forth or challenge, from pro-, forth, and vocare, to call, from vox, voice. English took it through French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 provocare「唤出、挑战」，由 pro-「向前」与 vocare「呼叫」构成，而 vocare 出自 vox「声音」；英语十四世纪经法语引入。

items.en: Vox meant voice, and it is the source of vocal, voice and the whole calling family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「声音」，是 vocal、voice 以及整个「呼叫」词族的来源。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon, and it built verbs such as invoke, evoke and revoke.
items.cn: 这个词意为呼叫、召唤，构成了 invoke、evoke、revoke 等动词。

items.en: The prefix meant forward or forth, so provocare pictured a call sent out towards someone.
items.cn: 前缀意为向前、向外，所以这个词的画面是把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.en: The verb meant to call forth, to challenge, and in law to appeal against a decision.
items.cn: 这个动词意为唤出、挑战，在法律中指对裁决提出上诉。

items.en: English adopted the verb through French; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语经法语采用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十四世纪」。

items.en: The sense of stirring anger became dominant later, while the neutral sense of causing a response survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 「激起怒气」后来越来越占主导，而「引起回应」的中性义在正式写作中仍存活。

note.en: The first group shares the call root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of causing and stirring.
note.cn: 第一组与「provoke」共享「呼叫」词根或只是形近；第二组是与「引起、激起」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of stirring someone or something up.
entries.definitionCN: 指激怒、挑起这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that stirs a reaction or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指挑衅的、引人反应的。

entries.definition: To call out a memory or feeling, with the prefix meaning out.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤出记忆或情感，前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: To call upon, as a law or a power, with the prefix meaning in.
entries.definitionCN: 指援引法律或力量，前缀意为「向内」。

entries.definition: To call back, hence to cancel a right or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指唤回，因而指撤销权利或规定。

entries.definition: The stock of words, from the same voice root.
entries.definitionCN: 指词汇总量，同出「声音」词根。

entries.definition: To annoy mildly, with less drama than provoke.
entries.definitionCN: 指轻度惹恼，戏剧性不如本词。

entries.definition: To set off an event or reaction, often mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发事件或反应，常带机械意味。

entries.definition: To wake a feeling or interest in someone.
To urge people towards violent or unlawful action.
entries.definitionCN: 指煽动人们采取暴力或违法行动。

entries.definition: To draw out a response or information, usually without anger.
entries.definitionCN: 指引出回应或信息，通常不含怒气。

entries.definition: To bother someone mildly and repeatedly.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the voice root, its four sibling verbs, and the neutral and angry branches of meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「声音」词根、它的四个兄弟动词，以及中性义与激怒义两条分支。

normal.en: Vox is voice, so provoke is to send a call out and wait for an answer.
normal.cn: vox 是「声音」，所以这个词是发出一声召唤，等着回应。

normal.en: Invoke, evoke and revoke share the same calling root with different prefixes.
normal.cn: invoke、evoke、revoke 与它共享同一「呼叫」词根，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Provoke a debate is neutral; provoke a crowd is not.
normal.cn: 「引发辩论」是中性说法，「激怒人群」则不是。

normal.en: Provocation and provocative are the noun and adjective of the same action.
normal.cn: 它的名词与形容词形式分别表示「挑衅」与「挑衅的」。

normal.en: Cold air can provoke a cough, which shows how wide the neutral sense reaches.
normal.cn: 冷空气能诱发咳嗽，可见中性义覆盖面之广。

abstract.en: To provoke is to open a door and refuse to say what is behind it.
abstract.cn: 激怒，就是打开一扇门却不说门后有什么。

abstract.en: Every provocation is a question the other person is expected to answer badly.
abstract.cn: 每一次挑衅，都是一个预期对方会答坏的问题。

abstract.en: A response called forth is not the same as a response forced in, and that difference is the word.
abstract.cn: 被唤出的回应与被塞进去的回应不同，这个差别就是这个词本身。

examples.en: The cartoon provoked angry letters from both sides.
examples.cn: 这幅漫画招致双方愤怒的来信。

examples.en: Her question provoked a thoughtful silence.
examples.cn: 她的问题引来一阵沉思的沉默。

examples.en: Dust can provoke an asthma attack in sensitive people.
examples.cn: 粉尘可能诱发敏感人群的哮喘发作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普罗沃克」——长杆一伸，水面荡开圈圈波纹：引发、激怒

root: 拉丁语 vox「声音」→ vocare「呼叫」→ provocare「唤出、挑战」（pro-「向前」+ vocare）；英语十四世纪经法语引入。与 evoke、invoke、revoke 同根不同前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all call something forth: anger, a challenge, a reaction, curiosity, emotion, criticism, a symptom and collective action.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把某物唤出：怒气、挑战、反应、好奇、情绪、批评、症状与集体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pole touches still water and rings spread outward from the point of contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：长杆触到静水，圈圈波纹从触点向外荡开。

branches.en: THE INVITATION TO ANGER: someone is deliberately stirred and expected to react.
branches.cn: 向怒气发出邀请：某人被有意激起，并被期待作出反应。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ANSWER: a report or a decision draws discussion, criticism or protest.
branches.cn: 公众的回应：报告或决定引出讨论、批评或抗议。

branches.en: THE SPARK OF CURIOSITY: interest appears because something strange is placed in view.
branches.cn: 好奇的火星：奇怪之物被摆在眼前，兴趣随之出现。

branches.en: THE SURFACING FEELING: fear, pity or laughter is brought up from below.
branches.cn: 浮上来的情绪：恐惧、怜悯或笑意从底下被带上来。

branches.en: THE LATENT EPISODE: a symptom starts, or a crowd is moved into action.
branches.cn: 潜伏的发作：症状启动，或人群被鼓动起来。

intro.en: Provoke is a Latin verb of calling, and the prefix is the piece that decides which way the call goes.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「呼叫」的拉丁动词，前缀决定这声呼唤朝哪个方向去。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vox, vocare and provocare; the pieces are well recorded, so no part of the word is marked uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vox、vocare、provocare；这些部件有清楚记录，这个词没有哪一部分标为存疑。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole calling family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个「呼叫」词族的源头。

items.example: It built invoke, evoke and revoke.
It sends the call out towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把呼唤朝某人发出去。

items.example: The verb carried both the neutral and the combative shades.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼有中性义与好斗色彩。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅；激怒；诱因」
由该动词加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动的」
由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「气人的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「挑衅地」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「挑衅者」（少用）

definition_zh: 室内的；户内的
definition_en: located inside a building rather than outside
core_image: 雨天的操场空了，体育馆的门里挤满了人
scene: 下了一整周的雨，体育课全搬进了馆里。 We played indoor games on rainy days.
sceneCN: 这里 indoor 是「室内的」（第 1 个义项：在建筑内部）；句意是下雨天我们玩室内游戏。

derivatives.zh: 义为「在室内」，由本词加 -s 构成，多作状语
义为「户外的」，与本词相反
义为「门」，是本词的后半部分

senses.title: Located inside a building
senses.definition: situated inside a building and not open to the sky
senses.definitionCN: 位于建筑物内部，不见天空
senses.example: We played indoor games on rainy days.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨天我们玩室内游戏。
senses.why: In- means within, and door names the boundary crossed, so indoor marks what lies on the inside of that boundary.
senses.whyCN: in- 意为「在内」，door 标出被跨过的那道边界，indoor 便指边界内侧的东西。

senses.title: Used only before a noun
senses.titleCN: 只作定语：用在名词之前
senses.definition: used as a modifier before a noun, never after the verb be
senses.definitionCN: 作定语修饰名词，不放在 be 动词之后
senses.example: The hotel has an indoor pool.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店有一个室内泳池。
senses.why: The bare form is a label on the doorpost; once the thing moves, English asks for indoors instead.
senses.whyCN: 光杆形式像门框上的标签；一旦东西动起来，英语就要求换成 indoors。

senses.title: Of weather or air, sheltered
senses.titleCN: 室内的：指空气、天气受遮蔽
senses.definition: describing the air or climate of a sheltered space, often in health talk
senses.definitionCN: 描述受遮蔽空间里的空气或气候，常用于健康话题
senses.example: Indoor air can be worse than the air in the street.
senses.exampleCN: 室内空气可能比街上更差。
senses.why: Health research measures what the walls trap, and the word names that trapped space.
senses.whyCN: 健康研究测的是墙内积聚的东西，这个词就命名那片被墙围住的空间。

senses.title: Of activity, taking place under a roof
senses.titleCN: 室内的：活动在屋顶之下进行
senses.definition: describing a sport or recreation played beneath a roof
senses.definitionCN: 指在屋顶下进行的运动或娱乐
senses.example: Basketball and badminton are indoor sports.
senses.exampleCN: 篮球和羽毛球是室内运动。
senses.why: Weather makes a game move its roof over it, and the word records that choice.
senses.whyCN: 天气逼着比赛搬进屋顶下，这个词记录的正是这一选择。

intro.en: Indoor is in plus door, meaning within the door of a house.
intro.cn: indoor 是 in 加 door，意为「在屋门之内」。

items.en: Dur and in existed separately: a door and a position inside.
items.cn: dur 与 in 各自独立：一个是门，一个是里面的位置。

items.en: The phrase within dore described staying inside a house.
items.cn: 短语 within dore 表示待在家里。

items.en: The compound in-door began to work as an adjective.
items.cn: 复合词 in-door 开始充当形容词。

items.en: The spelling settled as indoor, used before a noun.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 indoor，放在名词之前。

items.en: Modern sport, health studies and design made it common.
items.cn: 现代运动、健康研究与设计让它变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the door element; the near-meaning group holds words for sheltered spaces.
note.cn: 形近组共用 door 成分；近义组收表示有遮蔽空间的词。

entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在室内」，多作状语。
形容词，义为「户外的」，与本词相反。
形容词，义为「内部的」，共用 in 概念。

entries.definition: Of the inside of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，较正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the doorway as a line and the sports hall full of rain-day games.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把门口当作一条界线，并借雨中挤满人的体育馆。

normal.en: In plus door: if you are behind the door, you are indoor.
normal.cn: in 加 door：在门里面，就是室内的。

normal.en: Indoor before a noun; indoors for where you go: an indoor pool, but stay indoors.
normal.cn: indoor 放名词前，indoors 表在哪儿：an indoor pool，但说 stay indoors。

normal.en: Take away the roof and the word becomes outdoor.
normal.cn: 把屋顶掀掉，这个词就变成 outdoor。

normal.en: Rain moves the game inside, and an indoor sport is born.
normal.cn: 雨把比赛赶进屋，室内运动就此诞生。

normal.en: A door is thin, yet it divides two climates.
normal.cn: 一道门很薄，却分开了两种气候。

abstract.en: A wall is a decision about which weather to live in.
abstract.cn: 一堵墙，就是关于要在哪种天气里生活的决定。

abstract.en: Modern life moved far behind the door, and the word quietly records that move.
abstract.cn: 现代生活远远搬到了门后，这个词默默记下这一变迁。

abstract.en: Indoor air is still air, and what the walls keep out they also keep in.
abstract.cn: 室内的空气仍是一种空气：墙挡在外面，也关在里面。

examples.en: The children need more indoor activities in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天孩子们需要更多室内活动。

examples.en: There is an indoor market near the station.
examples.cn: 车站附近有一个室内市场。

examples.en: Indoor plants need less water in winter.
examples.cn: 室内植物在冬天需要的水更少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因朵」——因为下雨，花都搬到门里，成了室内的花。

root: in（在内）+ door（门，古英语 dur）→ 门内之物；同源表达 indoors、outdoor、doorway。

sensesIntro.en: Indoor begins at the doorway and names everything that lies inside it: rooms, air, sports and the grammar of a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: indoor 从门口开始，命名门内的一切：房间、空气、运动，以及它作定语的语法位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sports hall packed with people while rain falls outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：外面下雨，体育馆里挤满了人。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: the thing sits inside a building.
branches.cn: 空间线：东西位于建筑之内。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the word only stands before a noun.
branches.cn: 语法线：这个词只站在名词前面。

branches.en: HEALTH LINE: air trapped by walls gets measured.
branches.cn: 健康线：被墙围住的空气会被测量。

branches.en: SPORT LINE: the roof takes over from the sky.
branches.cn: 运动线：屋顶取代了天空。

branches.en: CONTRAST LINE: indoor always answers to outdoor.
branches.cn: 对照线：indoor 总与 outdoor 相对。

intro.en: A position prefix joined to a door word, producing an adjective of place.
intro.cn: 方位前缀接上「门」这个词，造出表地点的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Old English: in plus dur, the door; no Latin is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是古英语的 in 加 dur（门），此处不需拉丁语。

items.meaning: turning a place word into an adverb

definition_zh: 翻译；译文；转化；译作
definition_en: the act of turning words into another language, or the text produced that way
core_image: 一叠稿纸被搬到对岸，落地时已经换成另一种文字
scene: 出版社的编辑桌上有两叠稿纸，左边是原文，右边是译者交来的另一国文字。 The translation of the novel took her almost two years.
sceneCN: 这里 translation 是「翻译（这件事）」（第 1 个义项：把文字换成另一种语言）；句意为这部小说的翻译花了她将近两年。桌上一左一右的两叠稿纸正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ion 还原为动词，义为「翻译」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「译者」
名词加 -al 构成形容词，义为「翻译的；转化研究的」

senses.title: The act of rendering into another language
senses.definition: the work or process of expressing text in another language
senses.definitionCN: 把文本用另一种语言表达出来的工作或过程
senses.example: Translation demands patience as much as talent.
senses.exampleCN: 翻译既要有天分，也要有耐心。
senses.why: Latus means carried, so translation names the carrying of meaning from one tongue to another.
senses.whyCN: latus 意为「被搬运」，所以 translation 指的就是把意义从一种语言扛到另一种语言。

senses.title: A text in another language
senses.definition: the written result of translating, a text in the target language
senses.definitionCN: 翻译之后写出来的成品，即目标语言的文本
senses.example: I read the Chinese translation of the play.
senses.exampleCN: 我读了这个剧本的中文译本。
senses.why: Once the act is done, the load itself takes the name, and the finished text is called a translation.
senses.whyCN: 动作做完之后，那担货本身也得了这个名字，成品文本就叫译文。

senses.title: A change into another form or state
senses.definition: the process of changing something into a different form or result
senses.definitionCN: 某物变成另一种形式或结果的过程
senses.example: The translation of theory into practice is slow.
senses.exampleCN: 理论向实践的转化是缓慢的。
senses.why: Because the root only means carried across, any movement from one state to another can be called a translation.
senses.whyCN: 因为词根本身只表示「搬过去」，任何从一种状态到另一种的移动都可称为转化。

senses.title: Movement from one place to another
senses.definition: the removal of a person or thing to another place, especially a bishop to another see
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物移到另一处，尤指主教调任
senses.example: His translation to the northern diocese surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他调任北方教区让所有人都很意外。
senses.why: This is the earliest English sense, since the word first named the moving of a holy man to a new seat.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最早的义项，因为这个词最初指把神职人员搬到新的座位。

senses.title: Motion with no rotation
senses.definition: movement in which every point of a body shifts the same distance in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 物体上每个点都以相同距离向同一方向移动
senses.example: In pure translation, every point of the box moves alike.
senses.exampleCN: 在纯平动中，箱子的每个点移动得一模一样。
senses.why: Physics keeps the plain sense of carrying over: the whole body is carried to a new place without turning.
senses.whyCN: 物理保留了最朴素的「搬过去」义：整个物体被搬到新位置而不转动。

intro.en: The noun comes from Latin translatio, a carrying across, formed on latus, carried, and the prefix trans-, across.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语 translatio，意为「搬运过去」，由 latus（被搬运）与前缀 trans-（穿过）构成。

items.en: Latus is the past participle of ferre, to carry, and names the thing that has been carried.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre（搬运）的过去分词，指被搬过的那个东西。

items.en: Translatio means a transferring, first of goods or of a bishop, and later of meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语 translatio 意为转移，先指货物或主教，后指意义。

items.en: Old French translation keeps the sense of a transfer or removal.
items.cn: 古法语 translation 保留了转移、迁走的含义。

items.en: English uses the word for a bishop’s removal from the thirteenth century, and for rendering text from the sixteenth.
items.cn: 英语从十三世纪用它指主教调任，十六世纪起用它指翻译文本。

items.en: Modern science adds the mechanical sense of motion without rotation.
items.cn: 现代科学又添上「不旋转的移动」这一力学义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -lat- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words about the text and the work of rendering.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -lat- 词干，近义组汇集与译稿和转写工作相关的词。

entries.definition: a move from one place to another
to send a signal across a distance
a particular form of a text in another language
a translation or performance of a work
an explanation of what something means

normalIntro.en: Once you see latus, carried, the whole family becomes easy to place.
normalIntro.cn: 看到 latus（被搬运）之后，整个词族就好定位了。

normal.en: Translate is the verb, translation the noun, and translator the person.
normal.cn: translate 是动词，translation 是名词，translator 是人。

normal.en: The -tion ending marks a finished act or its product, so the noun can mean both the work and the text.
normal.cn: -tion 结尾标记已完成的行为或其产物，所以名词既可指工作也可指成品。

normal.en: Compare relation and transfer, which build on the same carried root.
normal.cn: 对比 relation 与 transfer，它们建在同一个「搬运」词根上。

normal.en: In a library, the shelf label usually means the finished book, not the labour.
normal.cn: 在图书馆里，这个标签通常指成品书，而不是那份劳动。

normal.en: The physics sense drops all language and keeps only the carrying.
normal.cn: 物理义抛开语言，只留下搬运这一层。

abstract.en: Picture two stacks of paper on one desk, one in each script.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张桌上两叠纸，各用一种文字。

abstract.en: Hear the soft rustle as one stack is laid down as the other.
abstract.cn: 听见一叠放下、另一叠成形的轻响。

abstract.en: Think of the bridge as invisible, and only the landing visible.
abstract.cn: 把桥想成看不见的，能看见的只有着陆。

examples.en: His translation of the poem keeps the rhyme of the original.
examples.cn: 他的译文保留了原诗的韵脚。

examples.en: The translation from idea to product took five years.
examples.cn: 从想法到产品的转化花了五年。

examples.en: She checked two translations before choosing one.
examples.cn: 她比较了两个译本之后才选定一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿斯雷神」——雷神把话跨过河送到对岸，就是翻译。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（穿过）+ latus（ferre「搬运」的过去分词），名词 translatio 经古法语进入英语；同族有 translate、transfer、relate

sensesIntro.en: The senses divide neatly between the act, the product, and the movement, because all three can be called a carrying across.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项在「行为」「成品」「移动」三处分开，因为这三样都能叫一次搬运。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of pages set down on the far bank in new letters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠稿纸在对岸落地，字已经换了。

branches.en: The labour sense, where the carrying is the work itself.
branches.cn: 劳动义：搬运本身就是那份工作。

senses.title: Graceful in manner

intro.en: Elegant comes from Latin elegans, a word for tasteful and choosy, built on eligere, to pick out; it reached English through French.
intro.cn: elegant 来自拉丁语 elegans，意为「有品味的、会挑选的」，其根是 eligere（挑出）；它经法语进入英语。

items.en: Eligere meant to pick out or choose, from ex plus legere, to gather.
items.cn: eligere 意为「挑出、选择」，由 ex 加 legere（收取）构成。

items.en: The participle elegans described someone who chooses well and so has fine taste.
items.cn: 分词 elegans 形容一个人会挑选，因而品味出众。

items.en: French borrowed the word for refined and handsome.
items.cn: 法语借入这个词，表示「精致的、俊雅的」。

items.en: English took it for manners and dress that show good taste.
items.cn: 英语借入它，指表现出好品味的举止与衣着。

items.en: Design and mathematics extended it to anything done with the fewest parts.
items.cn: 设计与数学把它扩展到一切「用最少部件完成」的事物上。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps elegance and its false friend elegy apart; the near-meaning group sorts grace, style and refinement.
note.cn: 形近组把 elegance 与易混的 elegy 分开；近义组区分 grace、style 与 refinement。

entries.definition: Smooth and flowing in movement; about the body rather than taste.

entries.definition: Fashionable and striking; more about current trend than restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「时髦的」，更看重当下潮流而非克制。

entries.definition: Polished by culture and training; the result of long cultivation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有修养的、精炼的」，是长期教养的结果。

entries.definition: Neat and well dressed, or clever; broader and more casual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「整洁漂亮的；聪明的」，更宽泛也更口语。
